implementation_notes: Go has no pool type because the channel is the pool: one buffered channel plus N worker goroutines per dependency bounds in-flight work, and a non-blocking send (select with default) is the fail-fast rejection path; this is the idiomatic realization and needs no dependency. Keep it when a blocking dependency must be isolated onto dedicated workers; when tasks are spawned per request instead of queued, the sibling semaphore variant is usually smaller.

variants.name: buffered channel + worker goroutines per dependency
variants.implementation_notes: Go has no pool type because the channel is the pool: one buffered channel plus N worker goroutines per dependency bounds in-flight work, and a non-blocking send (select with default) is the fail-fast rejection path; this is the idiomatic realization and needs no dependency. variants.idiom_name: buffered channel worker pool with select/default rejection
pitfalls: Spawning a goroutine per request before admitting it defeats the bound: goroutines are cheap but not free, so enqueue first and let workers admit the work.
A blocking send without a ctx or default branch parks the producer, turning the bulkhead into an unbounded wait; always give the send a cancellation path.
Channel capacity counts pending jobs, not running workers; bound both and drain the channel on shutdown or workers leak.
One channel per call site rather than per dependency silently multiplies the dependency's total concurrency.

variants.name: x/sync weighted semaphore and errgroup.SetLimit
variants.implementation_notes: Library form: semaphore.NewWeighted(n) implements weighted admission, Acquire(ctx, 1) gives the bounded wait driven by the context deadline and TryAcquire(1) the immediate rejection, with Release on every path; errgroup.SetLimit(n) bounds a fan-out of subtasks and blocks the launcher when full (backpressure), while TryGo offers the non-blocking variant. Prefer this over a channel worker pool when calls already suspend on I/O and no dedicated workers are needed.
pitfalls: Acquire blocks until the context is done; with context.Background it waits forever, so always pass the request context to make saturation bounded.
Release must be deferred immediately after a successful acquire; any early return in between leaks weight capacity.
Weighted permits allow Acquire(ctx, n) for n > 1, so capacity is the sum of weights, not the number of callers.
x/sync versions independently of the toolchain; SetLimit and TryGo are newer additions, so pin a module version that provides them.
